retrieval.summary: Two retailer-search providers (Serper primary, Brave fallback) plus an internal product_catalog table. Retailer results and catalog rows are merged into one candidate array via field-aliasing (adaptCatalogCandidate/mergeProductCandidates).

deduplication.method: EXACT MATCH ONLY: dedupe key is (a) exact id, then (b) exact normalized (lowercased) product URL.
deduplication.gap: There is NO brand+title+category fuzzy duplicate detection, NO image-hash duplicate detection, and NO cross-retailer canonical-product merge in production today. This is the exact gap this lab studies.

separateRetailerScopedIdentityKey.summary: A DIFFERENT, narrower key used elsewhere in commerce funnel logic (v127). Priority: (retailerId+sku) > canonicalized URL (tracking params stripped) > provider id (hash of raw URL, so trailing slash/case/param differences break it) > (retailer+normalized title). Comment at :320-327 explicitly documents that the provider-id tier had to be reordered because Serper/Brave synthesize `id` by hashing the RAW productUrl, which broke canonical-URL matching. This key is RETAILER-SCOPED throughout (every tier includes the retailer/source) - it never claims cross-retailer identity, which is exactly the gap this lab's resolver targets.

vectorEmbeddingStack.summary: No Pinecone/Milvus/pgvector import, no embedding-model API call, no ANN index found anywhere in the traced retrieval/ranking stages. Matching is text/attribute-based only. Confirms spec section 15's instruction not to assume reusable visual embeddings exist - Tier 3 (fuzzy/visual) is out of scope for this lab's V1 build.

crossFeatureIdentityAudit.method: Direct source read by a dedicated research pass over supabase/migrations, services/, types/, supabase/functions - this pass's own evidence, not inferred.

surfaces.identifier: (source, canonical_url) pair - the normalized retailer listing URL is the sole identity authority. No product-level key exists.
surfaces.sourceFile: supabase/migrations/20260830150000_user_commerce_watches.sql:27-37,103-105 (unique index on (user_id, canonical_url)); supabase/functions/scan-identify/watchlistCapability.ts:54-60 (WATCH_PROVIDER_REGISTRY limited to farfetch, kickscrew)
surfaces.designNote: Migration comment at :31-37 explicitly states source/canonical_url together ARE the identity, and that a canonicalProductKey or brand/title hash was considered and REJECTED as unstable.

surfaces.identifier: Closet items: client_id (locally client-generated, not a retailer/product id) - table has NO product_url/external_product_id/retailer field at all (pure fashion taxonomy). Saved Scans: row id; the products jsonb column is an opaque, untyped snapshot with no identity extraction or dedup.
surfaces.sourceFile: supabase/migrations/20260829203657_user_closet_items.sql:16-71; services/closetLibrary.js:128-198 (CLOSET_ITEM_TAXONOMY_FIELDS, explicit 'COMMERCE EXCLUSION BOUNDARY' comment at :172-180); supabase/migrations/20260617215307_create_saved_scans.sql:6-40; services/savedScansCloud.ts:27-322
surfaces.stableAcrossRetailers: N/A - Closet carries no commerce identity by design; Saved Scans never deduplicates by product

surfaces.identifier: computeDressingRoomDedupeKey - a room-scoped priority chain: closet_item_id > scan_id+selected_item_id > saved_scan_id > inspiration_item_id > provider_product_id > storage_bucket+path > image_digest > request_idempotency_key. Every key is suffixed ':room:{roomId}'.
surfaces.sourceFile: services/dressingRoomDedupe.ts:1-107 (module header explicitly: 'Never merges different colors/variants/retailers with distinct offers'); supabase/migrations/202605200001_persistent_style_objects.sql:17-79 (dressing_room_items/look_items tables); types/canonicalDressingRoomItem.ts:9-40
surfaces.stableAcrossSessions: room-scoped only - deterministic for the same room+source, not a durable cross-room or cross-surface identity by design

surfaces.identifier: productRef = commerce record's own id, else its purchase URL, else its image URL (documented as 'a correlation handle, never an authorization input'). Feeds the paid-generation idempotency key sha256(userId|productRef|garmentImageUrl|personImageDigest|requestGeneration).
surfaces.retailerSpecific: derivative - inherits whatever instability Commerce's own id/URL already has
surfaces.stableAcrossSessions: unknown/likely no - inherited directly from Commerce's per-response RecommendedProduct.id, which is provider-synthesized per request, not a durable identifier

crossFeatureIdentityAudit.conclusion: Every surface in K Scan today defines 'same product' differently, and every definition is either retailer-scoped, session/room-scoped, or (Closet) absent entirely. None is stable across retailers. This is precisely the incompatibility this lab's Style -> Variant -> Offer model is designed to eventually unify (design-only in V1; see design/ directory).
